title: 10,000-Row Logistics Inventory Table Cascading Re-Render Freeze
businessContext: A freight forwarding dispatch dashboard displays a live table of 10,000 shipments. When the operator types into a search input at the top of the page, keystrokes experience 800ms input lag, rendering the application unusable.
problemStatement: Every single keystroke updates search query state in the parent page component. Because the table row components are un-memoized and receive newly created inline arrow functions and object literals on every render, all 10,000 row components re-render and re-calculate DOM styles on every character typed.
constraints: Typing in the search input must feel instantaneous (under 16ms input latency).
Table must display filtered results responsively.
Must demonstrate proper use of React.memo, useMemo, useCallback, or virtualization.
candidateTasks: Diagnose the two major performance bottlenecks: cascading re-renders and un-virtualized DOM node count.
Apply `useMemo` for filtered dataset and `useCallback` or stable handler for `onSelect`.
Explain windowing/virtualization (e.g. `@tanstack/react-virtual` or `react-window`) to only render visible DOM rows.
hints: Creating inline arrow functions `<TableRow onSelect={() => ...} />` creates a new function reference on every render, defeating `React.memo(TableRow)`.
Even with React.memo, rendering 10,000 actual DOM nodes in the browser causes severe layout and style recalculation bottlenecks.

testCases.name: Eliminates cascading re-renders and bounds rendered nodes
testCases.explanation: Transforms heavy table to lightweight virtualized rendering.

alternativeApproaches: Using React 18 useTransition to mark filtering as non-urgent.
Server-side filtering with pagination / cursor fetching.
commonMistakes: Assuming React.memo alone solves rendering 10,000 DOM nodes.
Wrapping everything in useMemo without measuring overhead.
